articleTitle: Video bandwidth prediction by GEO satellite terminals for QoE
abstract: Video streaming applications rely on bandwidth to promptly send out request packets through IP routers such as geosynchronous (GEO) satellite terminals. For GEO satellite networks with a large number of terminals such as more than thousands of terminals per user beam, contention and bandwidth assignments are used to share the bandwidth among multiplexed satellite communications. Bandwidth requests and assignments play a significant role in video streaming applications and their end-user perceived video Quality of Experience (QoE), packets are queued inside a terminal when the current bandwidth assignment is not enough to send out request packets for large video bandwidth. Since a GEO satellite terminal’s request for bandwidth gets sent to its Gateway for its ground system through the satellite link, a GEO round trip delay for Bandwidth request and assignment can take more than 600 milliseconds. Previous works such as the Machine Learning (ML) based HTTP request arrival prediction by Pimpinella et al. utilized Random Forest Regressor, a ML algorithm in HTTP prediction [1]. In this work, we propose a Deep Learning (DL) prediction model-based Video TCP Request that is able to predict when the next video request packet will be issued by video streaming applications of a given satellite terminal which enable terminals to request Bandwidth just before it is needed and avoid waiting for the satellite round trip delay. The proposed solution is able to achieve a very low loss of 3.322x10-5 with our custom loss function, and above average in hitting 5- and 10-seconds accuracy window, using a univariate time series, which enables low computation inside the satellite terminal for distributed computing.

articleTitle: OpenLanes: network emulation system for mega-constellation networks
abstract: The deployment of mega-constellations with inter-satellite links has made space networking environments extremely complex, due to the significant number of potential paths and the regular topology changes. Each shift in the network topology necessitates a reassessment and adjustment of routing on the satellites. Because of this complexity, a rigorous testing process is demanded to evaluate network capabilities and mechanisms before they are deployed. To address this challenge, we developed OpenLanes, a comprehensive network emulation toolkit designed to assess satellite systems' networking capabilities. OpenLanes emulates network links across a large number of virtual nodes, providing a realistic environment for evaluating solutions in multi-layer satellite mega-constellation networking conditions. Additionally, it can integrate with external payload hardware, allowing for the evaluation of network components and their functionality in a controlled environment. Our versatile toolkit can also emulate various network types, including terrestrial, non-terrestrial, and hybrid networks. By using OpenLanes, we can ensure robust assessments and minimize the risk of unexpected, side-effects issues during in-orbit deployment.

articleTitle: Design and initial on-orbit testing of a commercial optical space data relay network
abstract: Kepler is deploying a commercial optical space data relay network providing real-time, high-bandwidth internet connectivity to LEO space, air, and ground users. The Kepler Network will be compatible with the SDA Optical Communications Standard, and interoperable with SDA-Standard-compatible networks such as the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA). In 2023, Kepler launched two satellites equipped with optical communications terminals (OCTs). These technology demonstrator satellites are in-orbit testbeds of critical technologies for the Kepler Network including optical intersatellite links (OISLs) and mesh internet protocol (IP) networking. Kepler achieved its first OISLs in June 2024, representing the first successful SDA-compatible links by a commercial company. The only other SDA-compatible OCTs launched to date have been those onboard the PWSA satellites. In this paper we describe the design of Kepler’s optical satellites, both the initial testbeds and the operational relay satellites, and the OCTs they host. We describe results of initial space-to-space testing, including pointing, acquisition, and tracking (PAT) sequence and resulting acquisition time, and how this is affected by the total uncertainty cone (TUC) size. Kepler is expanding the scope of its optical link testing, including longer-duration links and testing with partner space-to-ground and space-to-air SDA-compatible optical terminals.

articleTitle: Study on machine learning-based prediction of intensity fluctuations in horizontal optical propagation
abstract: This study investigates the potential of machine learning to predict signal power fluctuations in free-space optical communications, impacted by atmospheric fluctuations. Conducted over a 600-meter terrestrial link, optical reception intensities were recorded at a sampling rate of 10 kHz, then averaged to 1 kHz to reduce the computational load for subsequent machine learning processes. The study employed 80% of this data for training and 20% for validation. It was demonstrated that within the spatial coherence time of atmospheric turbulence, the fluctuations in received signal intensity can be accurately predicted using machine learning.

articleTitle: Development of wideband modulator and demodulator of LDM transmission for 21-GHz-band satellite broadcasting
abstract: We are developing a satellite broadcasting system that uses layered division multiplexing (LDM) transmission. It enables broadcasting services to be provided flexibly in accordance with the receiving quality. We have developed a wideband modulator and demodulator of LDM transmission for 21-GHz-band satellite broadcasting. This paper shows their specifications, structure, and transmission performance evaluated in a laboratory experiment.

articleTitle: Service provider agnostic adaptive coding and modulation system design
abstract: Commercial service providers (CSPs) are increasingly used to provide communications services to near-Earth science and exploration missions. CSPs commonly utilize modems that are designed to implement adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) in unique ways with modems from the same vendor. However, some missions cannot fly a matching vendor modem, either because the vendor only designs modems for terrestrial use, or the mission needs to fly a software defined radio. We present an ACM system design that allows missions to implement ACM on DVB-S2 compliant CSP links without needing to fly a modem from the same vendor the CSP uses. We implement and test our design in an emulated communications testbed. These tests demonstrate that our ACM system design can successfully adapt to link quality changes up to 6.12 dB/second.

articleTitle: Perspectives on building a NASA DSN-affiliated antenna
abstract: Over the past several years, much effort was devoted to upgrading the 21-m antenna at the Morehead State University, Kentucky, United States and making it into an affiliated station of the NASA Deep Space Network (DSN). This paper captures perspectives on what is required to convert a non-DSN ground station into an affiliated operational node of the Deep Space Network. Key desirable characteristics of an affiliated antenna are discussed, in comparison with a typical cross support antennas from other partner space agencies. One of the foremost considerations is having common interfaces to mission users. These interfaces range from the early process of service scheduling to the final stage of delivering telemetry, tracking and command data. Beside technical considerations, this paper also examines what is required in human resources and capital investment to turn a desire of being a DSN-affiliated antenna into a reality. These resources are needed not just for the initial development of capabilities, but also for sustaining the operations and services to mission users.

articleTitle: Analytical assessment of multi-beam LEO constellations using improved stochastic geometry models
abstract: This paper considers a framework for examining aspects of the trade-space in LEO constellations and their impact on link performance using stochastic geometry. The Poisson point process model over spherical surface is refined to provide a better match between a stochastic model and real-world, deterministic LEO constellations. The application of this model to quantify different aspects of the trade-space, such as the constellation size, altitude, orbital inclination, user-to-satellite elevation angle and user-terminal location is discussed. The paper also considers the pragmatic scenario where LEO satellites providing broadband access serve the coverage area using multiple, narrow beams. Techniques to assess impact of co-channel interference from the serving satellite to the user terminal’s spectral efficiency are discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization of HAPS placement in hybrid FSO/RF space-air-ground integrated networks
abstract: In the 6G era, non-terrestrial networks capable of providing communication services to the entire earth have garnered significant attention. As the area covered by satellites and airborne platforms such as high-altitude platform stations (HAPS) increases, the transmission capacity of the system needs to be increased. Therefore, the integration of free-space optical communications, which offer large capacity but are affected by atmospheric instability, with radio frequency communications, known for their stability but limited capacity, is expected to be a viable solution for satellite communications. In this paper, we propose a placement control method for HAPS that maximises the spectral efficiency of space-air-ground integrated networks. Simulations showed that the spectral efficiency of the system can be maximised by considering both the satellite orbits and the traffic demand distribution when deploying HAPS.

articleTitle: An experiment of improving accuracy of clock recovery on free space optical communications by initial wavefront multiplexing multibeam method
abstract: In free space optical communications, receiving light intensity fluctuated by atmospheric turbulence leads temporal signal distortion and increase of the bit error rate. For stable communications, a multibeam transmission is one of the effective solutions. In this study, we verify the effectiveness of the initial wavefront multiplexing multibeam method, by focusing on the amount of time jitter of the clock wave measured through optical path in turbulent environment. The experiment shows that the time jitter is decreased with the initial wavefront multiplexing multibeam method and indicates that this scheme has the effect to reduce the influence of atmospheric turbulence on optical communications system.

articleTitle: Sustained evaluation of AIS satellite reception channels (CH75, 76) via ALOS-2/SPAISE2 for assessing the economic viability of maritime satellite communications
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the adoption and performance of the newly established AIS channels, CH75 and CH76, over a decade. Using empirical data, we demonstrate that these channels have progressively enhanced data collection capabilities in congested maritime areas. While the findings show a notable improvement in the effectiveness of satellite constellations through the use of these new channels, they also highlight the need for ongoing refinement to fully optimize their performance.

articleTitle: ILKA - a lightweight KU-band antenna solution for mobile satellite communication: experimental evaluation
abstract: With interest growing for small and low-cost user terminals for the consumer market, innovative and lightweight manufacturing processes for antenna systems are needed more than ever. In this paper, we introduce a novel design and lightweight manufacturing process for very-small-aperture terminals fitting backpack requirements. The prototype antenna system was characterized in a controlled laboratory environment to validate its surface accuracy and RF performance. Additionally, an end-to-end over-the-air field test, utilizing real GEO satellite capacity, was conducted to assess its performance in a real-world deployment. The results demonstrate that the prototype closely replicates the performance of existing commercial off-the-shelf user terminal solutions.

articleTitle: Satellite communication link anomaly identification assisted by AI/ML
abstract: Like all communication systems, satellite communication often encounters anomalies from a variety of impairments, such as weather and interferences. Timely anomaly identification and resolution is critical in improving the quality of service. With the advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) tools, we explore how to leverage AI/ML to assist satellite communication anomaly identifications and resolutions. In this paper, we present our work on developing the AI assisted tool using an efficient convolutional neural network (CNN) model with multi-classification architectures, where various communication link parameters are classified in a single model. Optimizations are made to the activation function, pre-processing of input data, as well as the loss function for back-propagation. The model was trained using the hybrid data training approach consisting of both field data and simulated data. The model was tested using various link scenarios for both RF and lasercom links. Preliminary results showed 90% or higher confidence levels for most space-ground RF links and 70% or higher for lasercom space-ground links.

articleTitle: Repurposable payloads: concept, design, and initial results
abstract: This paper introduces “repurposable payloads”, a new concept that transforms satellite payloads into versatile, all-purpose servers in space, optimized for efficient operations across multiple services, such as earth observation data processing and telecommunication network functions. Utilizing a compact, generic operating system and its software libraries, our system offers a common platform where different dedicated peripherals such as antennas or inter-satellite link modems can be integrated, and on top of which multiple applications can be installed and executed. We also detail a high-level architecture, illustrating its advantages in terms of enhanced customization flexibility for on-board processing. We provide an initial proof-of concept design, highlighting the best practices in implementation and an initial assessment of the new system. The evaluation results indicate promising performance, paving the way for a shift towards greater adaptability in satellite network design and functionality.

articleTitle: Early commercialization and system evolution for HAPS direct-to-mobile-phone service - traffic-control method taking into account QoS in non-terrestrial networks linking GEO satellites to HAPSs
Enhanced demodulator for 5G NTN using spatio-temporal attention convolutional autoencoder and Akida Brainchip SNN
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to overcoming challenges in 5G and 6G mobile satellite systems (MSS) in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), focusing on Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) issues in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) that connect directly with handheld devices. We utilize a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Spatio-Temporal Attention Network (STAN) autoencoder, which is then converted into a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) using Brainchip Akida’s Meta TF Software Framework. This integration of neuromorphic processing aims to enhance energy efficiency, reduce computational demands, and increase data transmission rates, optimizing Channel State Information (CSI) in compliance with 3GPP standards. Our STAN-CNN-SNN architecture achieves a 85% reduction in computational requirements, leading to decrease in power consumption, and increase in data rates within the C-Band spectrum. Simulations with LEO satellite MSS parameters demonstrate significant advancements in communication systems. The numerical results demonstrates substantial computational reductions with minimal capacity trade-offs.

articleTitle: SD-SAT: software-defined multi-constellation satellite communication traffic management framework
abstract: As Satellite Communication (SATCOM) continues to expand rapidly, the need for dynamic and resilient traffic management solutions tailored to large-scale SATCOM environments is becoming increasingly critical. To address these SATCOM challenges, we introduce the SD-SAT framework, a hierarchical, distributed Software-Defined Networking (SDN) enabled network resource and traffic management solution designed specifically for SATCOM networks. The SD-SAT architecture tackles key issues of scalability, flexibility, and efficiency by integrating multiple SDN controllers across different layers of the system. Within our SD-SAT framework, SDN controllers for individual satellite constellations are aggregated into a "control resource pool", which is managed by an upper-layer SDN control plane. This upper layer ensures global coordination and management, leveraging a distributed cluster of autonomous SDN controllers to enhance coverage, scalability, and resiliency. Additionally, we present a seamless SDN controller migration method that facilitates smooth transitions and load balancing for distributed SDN controllers within the network. The SD-SAT framework not only integrates seamlessly with an existing SATCOM infrastructure but also optimizes resource management and traffic handling across multiple constellations. By adapting distributed SDN control methodologies to the unique demands of SATCOM, the SD-SAT architecture provides a scalable, efficient solution that significantly enhances global connectivity and resource utilization.

articleTitle: Real-time in-lab evaluation of indirect satellite connectivity with the SeRANIS beyond 5G demonstrator
abstract: Indirect satellite connectivity combines terrestrial base stations and satellite backhaul links to extend mobile network coverage where terrestrial transport networks are lacking. Satellite backhaul via low Earth orbit (LEO) constellations offers reduced latency compared to geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) satellites. However, latency is higher and more variable than typical requirements for 5G and Beyond 5G (B5G) systems, which raises questions about the quality of experience (QoE) in integrated networks. This paper presents the Seamless Radio Access Networks for Internet of Space (SeRANIS) B5G demonstrator, an in-lab solution that combines a complete 5G system, an end-to-end satellite emulator, and tools for testing typical mobile network services. The demonstrator can switch between terrestrial and satellite backhaul, offering the opportunity to evaluate and compare performance between backhaul solutions. The performance of a video call/conference service is analysed under different network conditions in terrestrial and satellite backhaul scenarios. The paper shows objective metrics and the results of a subjective test on transmission quality conducted on 19 subjects. Results show a similar QoE between terrestrial and LEO backhaul for a video call/conference service, confirming that LEO backhaul is a viable solution to mitigate the “digital divide” affecting communities in rural or remote areas.

articleTitle: The international space station, optical communications, and delay tolerant networking: towards a solar system internet architecture
abstract: As Delay Tolerant Networking (DTN) matures as a software product its use cases have extended to infrastructural and architectural studies, bringing DTN closer to a widespread, operational technology. While it is known that a DTN can be configured, given complete information about a system of nodes, to provision a system with a complete network capability, what remains is to tackle practical considerations such as scalability, networking best practices, and how to establish service providers. In this paper, we document progress towards a scalable DTN architecture that was tested across multiple organizational and project boundaries; our approach was tested across nodes flying on the International Space Station (ISS) connected to a ground network. The network consists of four main network areas: the ISS, the White Sands Complex (WSC), the Mission Cloud Platform (MCP), and NASA’s Huntsville Operations Support Center (HOSC). The connections on the ground (WSC, MCP, and HOSC) are straightforward technically, but represent administrative and non-technical challenges that had to be overcome. The connection from the ISS to WSC was realized through a hybrid optical/RF means. In particular, NASA’s Integrated Laser Communications Relay Demonstration (LCRD) can form a relay from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) to the Earth, and was used in conjunction with the LCRD LEO User Modem and Amplifier Terminal (ILLUMA-T) on the ISS to form a link to one of three geographically diverse ground stations. A major goal was to achieve communications while keeping the ISS nodes unaware of ground station choices and scheduling. These disparate links were networked using High-rate DTN (HDTN), which enabled the desired architecture. The network architecture, tests, HDTN performance metrics, and general observations made are all discussed in detail, including a discussion on the successful utilization of the DTN security standard known as DTN Bundle Protocol Security (BPSec). We conclude with suggestions for next steps, and in particular focus on extending this architecture to the Near Space Network (NSN) and the upcoming LunaNet.

articleTitle: Advances on multi-transmission reception point over non-terrestrial networks for 6G
abstract: This paper explores user connectivity at the periphery of satellite beams, focusing on Very Small Aperture Terminals (VSATs) that may exhibit varying velocities. All beams providing coverage operate within the same frequency band, leading to the adoption of the multi-transmission reception point strategy (mTRP) to serve these users. Under this strategy, the User Equipment (UE) is concurrently linked to multiple New Radio (NR) nodes transmitting identical information. In our investigation, a UE is connected to two Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites, and we assess the performance of the Physical Downlink Shared Channel (PDSCH) in 5G-NR under this configuration. With both satellites transmitting the same packet, the probability of coverage outage due to UE mobility is reduced, as the UE transitions between the outer coverage areas of the two satellites. To enhance UE connectivity and minimize handovers, a packet duplication strategy is employed with the mTRP framework. Pre-coding techniques are utilized by both GEO satellites to mitigate channel effects, with each satellite adhering to a non-coherent mTRP strategy, meaning each channel retains only its own information. Simulation results are presented, and the implications of the findings are discussed.

articleTitle: Machine learning based throughput prediction in 5G NR non-terrestrial networks using system-level simulator
abstract: The ability to accurately predict a network’s throughput can enable mobile operators to allocate resources efficiently and improve the overall user experience. Nonetheless, the multidimensional parameter space involving such a network-level performance metric requires careful analyses of the underlying parameters and cross-layer dependencies. This paper presents a study on evaluation of classical machine learning algorithms for predicting the throughput in 5G NR Non-Terrestrial Networks using data from system level simulations. The study was conducted in three stages, namely dataset generation, dataset validation and visualization, and model evaluation. The results provide confidence in usage of system simulations for training and evaluation of machine learning algorithms. Furthermore, analyses show that techniques such as Random Forest Regression can prove to be quite effective and robust in throughput prediction.

articleTitle: A proactive adaptation of coding and modulation scheme to mitigate adjacent system interference in large LEO constellations
abstract: As multiple LEO satellite constellations are deployed, the likelihood of an in-line event (ILE, or a conjunction) between the satellites of different system providers operating on the same frequency but from different constellations increases. The ILE causes heightened interference at the victim receiver. In this paper we propose three schemes for mitigating the ILE-induced interference. Our first proposal relates to the adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) through which the transmitter of the affected system can lower the modulation and coding scheme (MCS) rate to counteract the reduced signal to interference ratio (SIR). However, this conventional ACM process suffers from latency due to the round-trip time (RTT) over the LEO links. We introduce a Proactive ACM (P-ACM) scheme that detects the onset of an ILE and promptly takes corrective action without the delay of multiple RTTs. Our proposed approach is more agile in responding to the ILE, thereby mitigating the impact of the ILE in terms of spectral efficiency (SE) and the latency. Our second proposal applies the successive interference cancellation (SIC) to address the impact of the interference at the physical layer receiver. This SIC scheme is effective when it matters the most – i.e., when the interference is stronger in the received power compared to the desired signal. Finally, our third proposal introduces cooperation between the two co-channel satellite systems that can mutually interfere. We conduct an analysis of the SIR during the ILE and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approaches through multiple simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Automated end-to-end spacecraft connectivity across diverse links
abstract: An increasing variety of communications services are available to space missions. Yet varying standards between providers hinder adoption due to the complexity of managing configurations for each communication pathway. We present a software framework which alleviates this issue by automatically establishing end-to-end communications during contacts with a provider. The proposed development configures spacecraft protocols at the physical, link, and network layers. The spacecraft remains reachable at the same IP address regardless of the active provider. Underlying protocols and routes are abstracted, allowing the user to simply send data to a destination with the framework ensuring its delivery. We evaluate a full implementation of the framework in laboratory experiments conducted on an emulated communications testbed. These tests demonstrate data delivery across three different services with rapid (<20s) reconfiguration as the spacecraft transitions between providers.

articleTitle: mioty superiority over both LoRa-versions in satellite-IoT applications
abstract: Low power wide area networks (LPWANs) represent a special case of the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, which aims at supporting massive access for remotely deployed IoT devices. The target application of such devices lies typically in the field of sensors with limited size and battery capacity as well as low data rate transmissions. Correspondingly, the transmit power of these sensors is very low while the distance between the transmitter and the (terrestrial) receiver can span tens of kilometres, which leads to a typically very low signal quality and critical link budget. Moreover, the large number of sensors transmitting their data packets at random times over the same radio resource poses a challenge with respect to co-channel interference. In order to cope with the aforementioned challenges of low signal quality and strong co-channel interference, multiple commercial products have been developed in the past for terrestrial applications. For terrestrial IoT applications two well-known systems areLoRaandmioty. In this work, we evaluate some comparisons between LoRa and mioty and apply the results to direct-to-satellite communications. LoRa has addressed some shortcomings of their waveform design with the updated variant LoRa FHSS. However, in some key aspects that also (but not exclusively) apply to satellite communications mioty still outperforms LoRa.
